chief_complaint: facial cheek pressure and green nasal discharge >10 days
hpi_details: 26-year-old female presents with 12 days of persistent purulent green nasal discharge, bilateral maxillary facial pressure that worsens when bending forward, and decreased sense of smell. Started as a regular cold but instead of improving, her symptoms worsened on day 7 ('double sickening').
ideas: She thinks mucus from an initial cold became trapped and turned into an infected pocket inside her cheekbones.
concerns: She is worried that the pounding facial pain and brain fog will keep her from staring at her computer screen and cause her to miss a crucial work deadline.
expectations: She hopes to receive a prescription for antibiotics and a potent nasal spray to relieve the sinus pressure immediately.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Acute Bacterial Rhinosinusitis evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Acute Bacterial Rhinosinusitis is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management follows an evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for acute bacterial rhinosinusitis: oral Amoxicillin-Clavulanate for 5-7 days, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: facial cheek pressure and green nasal discharge >10 days
Key HPI features: 26F with 12 days of persistent purulent green nasal discharge and maxillary pressure worsening when bending forward. Exhibits 'double sickening' (worsening on day 7).
Objective/Exam findings: Temp 37.5C. Anterior rhinoscopy shows purulent discharge from the middle meatus and swollen turbinates. Maxillary sinus tenderness present.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Acute Bacterial Sinusitis.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Viral sinusitis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

Ignoring critical warning signs such as: periorbital swelling, visual changes, or neurological signs, which suggest orbital or intracranial extension requiring urgent imaging and escalation rather than routine antibiotics.
management_principles: Prescribe oral Amoxicillin-Clavulanate for 5-7 days for suspected acute bacterial rhinosinusitis.
Recommend supportive care including saline nasal irrigations and intranasal corticosteroids.
Advise returning if symptoms worsen or if alarming signs (e.g., visual changes, severe headache) develop.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with facial cheek pressure and green nasal discharge for more than 10 days. 26-year-old female presents with 12 days of persistent purulent green nasal discharge, bilateral maxillary facial pressure that worsens when bending forward, and decreased sense of smell. Started as a regular cold but instead of improving, her symptoms worsened on day 7 ('double sickening').
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: Temp 37.5C. Anterior rhinoscopy shows purulent discharge from the middle meatus bilaterally and swollen, erythematous turbinates. Tenderness to percussion over maxillary sinuses.
reference_soap.plan: Prescribe oral Amoxicillin-Clavulanate 875/125 mg BID for 5-7 days. Recommend saline nasal irrigations and intranasal corticosteroids for symptomatic relief.

learning_objectives: Recognize the clinical presentation of Acute Bacterial Rhinosinusitis (symptoms >10 days or 'double sickening' pattern).
Select appropriate first-line antibiotic therapy (Amoxicillin-Clavulanate) according to guidelines.
Differentiate bacterial rhinosinusitis from viral upper respiratory infections.

teaching.one_liner: Bacterial sinus infection causing facial pressure and green nasal discharge lasting over 10 days.
red_flags: Periorbital swelling, erythema, or visual changes (diplopia, decreased acuity) — concerning for orbital cellulitis
Severe frontal headache with altered mental status, neck stiffness, or focal neurological signs — concerning for intracranial extension
High fever with a toxic appearance

must_ask.say: How many days has this lasted?

history.answer: I've had thick greenish nasal discharge and a heavy, aching pressure in both cheeks for the past twelve days.
It all started twelve days ago and hasn't gone away since.
It felt like a regular cold at first and seemed to ease up a bit, but around day seven it suddenly got much worse.
It has been thick, cloudy, and dark green, but there is no foul or rotten smell to it.
Both sides of my nose are completely stuffed up, and the thick mucus comes out of both nostrils.
No, I haven't noticed any blood or nosebleeds, and my face does not feel numb at all.
No, I haven't had itchy eyes, an itchy nose, sneezing fits, or watery eyes.
No, it hasn't varied by season, and it doesn't get triggered by dust, pollen, pets, or cold air.
I have a heavy pressure across both cheekbones that throbs worse when I bend over, but my upper teeth don't ache.
Yes, my sense of smell has been noticeably dull since the congestion worsened.
I've felt slightly warm and feverish over the last few days, but I haven't had high fevers or shaking chills.
No, my eyes aren't swollen or red, my vision is completely clear, and I don't have a severe headache or stiff neck.
I've been breathing through my mouth because of the blockage, but I don't snore heavily or stop breathing in my sleep.
I constantly feel mucus dripping down the back of my throat, which makes me clear my throat and cough a bit, but I'm not wheezing.
No, I haven't used any nasal decongestant sprays or steroid sprays.
No, I don't have asthma, and painkillers like aspirin or ibuprofen have never made me short of breath.
No, I haven't had any head or facial injuries, no sinus surgeries, and no clear watery fluid leaking from my nose.
No, I haven't had any dental work recently, and I have no tooth pain or gum swelling.
I've never had allergic rhinitis, asthma, or eczema, and no one in my family has allergies either.
I thought the cold I had last week never drained out and turned into a rotten infection trapped in my cheeks.
I'm really worried that this pounding facial pressure will keep me from working and make me miss a major project deadline this week.
I was hoping you could give me a course of antibiotics and a strong prescription spray so my face stops throbbing.
I don't have any chronic medical illnesses.
I have never had surgery or been admitted to a hospital.
I'm not taking any regular medications, over-the-counter remedies, or supplements.
I don't have any allergies to medications as far as I know.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used vape products.
I drink socially on occasion, about one glass of wine or beer once or twice a month.
I work as an office clerk and live in an apartment with a roommate.
Both my parents and my siblings are healthy with no history of sinus or respiratory problems.
My last period started two weeks ago on a normal 28-day cycle, we use condoms, and there is no chance of pregnancy.

exam.finding: The patient is alert, mildly uncomfortable, and in no acute respiratory distress.
Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, pulse 76 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, SpO2 99% on room air, and temperature 37.5°C.
Moderate tenderness elicited upon percussion and palpation over bilateral maxillary sinuses; frontal sinuses are nontender.

Anterior rhinoscopy reveals swollen erythematous turbinates with purulent green drainage from bilateral middle meatuses; posterior oropharynx demonstrates mild cobblestoning and purulent postnasal discharge.
No periorbital edema or erythema; extraocular movements are intact and painless bilaterally, pupils are equal and reactive, and visual acuity is preserved.
Both tympanic membranes are intact and translucent with crisp light reflexes and no middle ear effusion.
Small, nontender, mobile anterior cervical lymph nodes are palpable bilaterally without supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.
Neck is supple with full passive flexion; Kernig and Brudzinski signs are absent.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally on auscultation without wheezing, crackles, or rhonchi.
